assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on Katori's magic-wavelength lattice concept and brought to systematic uncertainties near 1e-18 by Ye's group, redefined the limit of time and frequency measurement. The work is original, conceptually clear and broad in impact: tests of fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and the coming redefinition of the second.
assessment.attribution: Two-person credit is clean: Katori proposed and first realized the magic-wavelength lattice; Ye drove the strontium clock to record accuracy and stability. Other clock groups (ion clocks, NIST and PTB) contributed related precision work, but the lattice-clock invention itself is well localized to these two.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently by many laboratories over more than a decade, with international comparisons of clocks. The 2005 prize covered the frequency comb, which makes this a natural, timely successor rather than a premature choice.
uncertainties: Overlap with the earlier recognition of frequency-comb and ion-clock work could be read as incremental by some members.
The formal redefinition of the second has not yet happened, so the full practical impact is still developing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED turned superconducting artificial atoms coupled to microwave resonators into a platform for strong coupling, dispersive readout and the transmon, and underpins current quantum processors. The scientific idea is clear and has lasting consequences. I know this field closely and judge its importance as very high.
assessment.attribution: The 2004 theory (Blais, Huang, Wallraff, Girvin, Schoelkopf) and the Yale experiments, together with the transmon, share the credit. Schoelkopf, Girvin and Blais form a defensible theory-plus-experiment set, but Wallraff, who did the first strong-coupling experiment, and Devoret, already honoured, complicate the allocation.
assessment.maturity: Replicated and extended by dozens of groups, and technologically mature. The weakness is timing: the 2025 prize recognized superconducting-circuit quantum behaviour, so a second prize in the same area so soon is a real consideration. I also have close professional ties to this field and must disclose them (Chalmers and WACQT), which tempers my ranking despite the strong merit.
uncertainties: Whether the committee wishes to honour superconducting circuits again straight after 2025.
Attribution among Wallraff, Schoelkopf, Girvin and Blais is not fully settled by the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realized Hubbard-type models, the superfluid-Mott transition and fermionic many-body states, creating the field of analogue quantum simulation. The theoretical blueprint and the experiments are original, and the impact on many-body physics is lasting.
assessment.attribution: Zoller (with Jaksch, Cirac and others) supplied the key proposals; Bloch's group and Greiner's early Mott-insulator experiment (Bloch group at the time) and Esslinger's Fermi-Hubbard work carried them out. I propose Bloch, Esslinger and Zoller, but Greiner's role and the contributions of the other proposal authors (e.g. Jaksch) remain a real allocation question.
assessment.maturity: Replicated widely and mature after more than two decades, with quantum gas microscopes extending the work. Recognition is timely, though 2001 and 2012 prizes in adjacent cold-atom topics narrow the unexplored ground.
uncertainties: Credit for the Mott-insulator experiment versus later quantum-gas-microscope work.
Zoller also appears in other candidates, which affects how a combined prize could be assembled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum key distribution turned the no-cloning principle into a practical security primitive and founded much of quantum information science. The BB84 idea is simple, original and has had large technological and conceptual impact.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard are the clear authors of BB84. Ekert's entanglement-based protocol (1991) is a distinct, independently motivated contribution and could justify a third seat; Wiesner's earlier conjugate-coding idea is not on the supplied list. I limit the proposal to two to keep the allocation tight.
assessment.maturity: Commercial and field deployments and satellite links confirm viability, and the 2022 prize on entanglement tests lessens the foundations argument but not the cryptographic one. Timing is acceptable but not urgent.
uncertainties: Whether physics (as opposed to computer science or cryptography) is the correct home for this prize.
The relative weight of Ekert's contribution is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators opened a major research area of topological band theory, with helical edge states and a link to Majorana physics. The theory is original and the experimental realization in HgTe is clear.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele supplied the theory and the Z2 classification; Molenkamp's group observed the quantum spin Hall effect in HgTe following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal. Zhang is deceased, so Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang cannot be credited in a prize and that gap is sensitive. Kane, Mele and Molenkamp is a reasonable set from the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Independently confirmed in many materials, including 3D topological insulators, and mature after almost two decades. The 2016 prize recognized topological phase transitions in a related but distinct sense.
uncertainties: Attribution gap from the BHZ proposal and from the 3D topological insulator experiments.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene exhibited correlated insulators and superconductivity in a tunable flat band, creating moire quantum matter as a platform for correlated electrons. The originality and impact are high.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the flat band at the magic angle; Jarillo-Herrero's group observed the correlated and superconducting states. This theory-plus-experiment pairing is defensible, but Cory Dean's group and the Kim and Yacoby groups also contributed to early confirmations.
assessment.maturity: Strong replication across many groups, but the nature of the superconductivity is not settled and the interpretation is still evolving, so recognition may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: The mechanism of the superconductivity is unresolved.
Contributions from other experimental groups complicate credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Precision measurements of the CMB anisotropy power spectrum fixed the geometry, composition and age of the universe, establishing the standard cosmological model with high accuracy. The scientific impact is large and the result is clear.
assessment.attribution: WMAP leadership (Bennett as PI), the theoretical and parameter analysis (Spergel) and the experimental design (Page) are plausible contributors; Puget (Planck) and the COBE laureates of 2006 are in the surrounding history. Large-collaboration credit is hard to localize, and I am less well placed to judge cosmology in detail.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently by WMAP, Planck and ground-based experiments, so maturity is high. The 2006 and 2019 prizes covered related cosmology, which makes the incremental case less obvious.
uncertainties: Credit within large collaborations is difficult to separate.
I have limited expertise in cosmological analysis, so my confidence is lower here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 2012 discovery of the Higgs boson by ATLAS and CMS completed the Standard Model's scalar sector and is among the most important experimental results in physics. The significance is unquestionable, and the 2013 prize honoured the theoretical prediction only.
assessment.attribution: Credit is spread over thousands of collaborators and the accelerator builders. Gianotti, Jenni and Virdee are plausible spokespeople and conceivers of the experiments, but Della Negra and Evans are equally defensible. The Nobel statutes' limit of three makes any selection contested.
assessment.maturity: Recognition is long overdue in terms of time, and the measurements are confirmed by two independent experiments. The main obstacle is the allocation of credit, not scientific maturity.
uncertainties: No fair three-person allocation exists for the experimental discovery.
Whether to recognize the machine, the detectors or leadership roles.
